name: Roast Spaghetti Squash with Turkey-Bell Pepper Sauté & Peanut Sauce

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to 260°C (500°F) and place rack in the center position. Line two baking sheet pans with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 medium spaghetti squash
3 limes
3 (2 ½ cm) pieces ginger root
3 red bell peppers

instructions.primary_message: Trim each spaghetti squash, halve lengthwise, and scrape out the seeds. Rub the inside of the squash with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Arrange halves, cut-side down, on the baking sheets.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ tbsp neutral vegetable oil
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 25-30 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice limes into a small bowl.
Peel and mince ginger. Add to the bowl with the lime juice along with peanut butter, water, soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, sugar, and spices. Whisk to combine the peanut sauce and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ cup natural peanut butter
3 tbsp water
3 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp chili-garlic sauce
1 tbsp brown sugar
¾ tsp turmeric, ground
¾ tsp curry powder
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bell pepper, turkey, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 5-6 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp neutral vegetable oil
1.02 kg ground turkey
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add half of the peanut sauce to the pot and stir to combine. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm. (Reserve remaining peanut sauce for serving.)

Remove squash from the oven and allow to cool slightly, about 5 minutes. Scrape the inside of the squash with a fork to separate into spaghetti-like strands. (Use an oven mitt or towel to hold it with your other hand.)
To serve, divide squash and turkey sauté between plates or bowls. Drizzle with reserved peanut sauce and enjoy!
